children: , the Swiss pharmaceutical and oncology giant, rocketed approximately 6% to $161.10 Tuesday after remibrutinib cleared two major Phase 3 tests in multiple sclerosis. The oral drug delivered fewer relapses and brain lesions than teriflunomide without raising the liver-safety concerns investors feared.

The upside may stretch beyond one clinical victory. Novartis said pooled results pointed to slower disability progression, giving remibrutinib another potential edge in a massive treatment market. The medicine is already sold as Rhapsido for chronic hives, but second-quarter sales were only $64 million. Full results arrive in October, with worldwide regulatory submissions set to follow.

The chart shows exactly how aggressively investors are pricing that promise. At $161.10, Novartis trades 23.13% above its $130.84 GF Value estimatea serious premium that leaves little room for disappointment. The rally also shows investors separating remibrutinib from eight suspended rap-cel studies following three deaths tied to severe immune reactions. Rap-cel is a different cell therapy, while two deaths in the remibrutinib trials were ruled unrelated to treatment. For now, the market sees one troubled programand one potential blockbuster moving sharply forward.

title: Novartis Jumps 6% as MS Drug Meets Goals in Two Phase 3 Trials
